text:
Priya: Quick sync — our forecast model keeps under-predicting short bursts for a subset of tenants (8-12%). Need to align model calibration with the autoscaler handshake. Anyone seen this in telemetry?
Sam: Yep saw that last week during the app launch spike. raw model output looked fine but admission dropped too early. :grimacing:
Diego: I think the issue is the aggregation window. Model uses 5m windows, autoscaler uses 1m. mismatch causes late pre-warm.
Mina: Can we add a short-term burst factor on top of model forecast? e.g. effective = max(model, EWMA_recent * (1+burst_pct))
Priya: That seems reasonable. we should keep it conservative so we don't over-provision. propose burst_pct default 0.15, tunable per-tenant.
Sam: Also need metric for forecast_error by lead_time. add buckets 0-10%, 10-25%, >25% so we can alert. @Taylor can you add to the dashboard?
Taylor: yep will add error buckets and a histogram for lead_time. ETA EOD.
Diego: ops handshake concerns: if autoscaler sees model forecast + burst factor, how do we guarantee operator isn't double-prewarming (operator warmup + autoscaler prewarm)? we need a handoff contract.
Priya: Handshake idea: forecast service emits "forecast_intent" with fields: forecast_value, confidence, horizon_s, and a lease_ttl. operator consumes intent and responds with a reservation token when it applies prewarm. If not acknowledged within lease_ttl, autoscaler falls back to reactive mode.
Mina: love that. keep lease_ttl short (30s-60s) to avoid stale intents. also add a "applied_variant" tag so we can trace which kernel/quantization was used.
Sam: example intents (pseudo):
```json
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "forecast": 32,
  "horizon_s": 300,
  "confidence": 0.7,
  "burst_pct": 0.15,
  "lease_ttl_s": 45
}
```
Diego: on the operator side, we need an idempotent accept API: `POST /v1/intents/{id}/accept` returns reservation token or a rejection with reason. operator should be able to include "estimated_ready_s".
orch-bot: autoscaler: canary applied - forecast_intent consumer bound to pool p-dedicated-canary-7 (rollout 10%).
Mina: nice. can we also emit a telemetry signal when operator delays > lease_ttl so autoscaler can switch to fallback path?
Priya: yes, fallback path should immediately allow reactive prewarm and mark a short cooling period to avoid thrash. we also want to surface tenant-level cost impact when fallback engages.
Sam: telemetry query to add to dashboard (promql-ish):
```
sum by(tenant) (increase(forecast_intent_rejected[15m]))
/
sum by(tenant) (increase(forecast_intent_total[15m]))
```
Taylor: adding both the error buckets and the rejected/total ratio.
Diego: one more: calibration loop. we should periodically reweight model vs ewma using recent realized delta. simple logistic update: alpha = clamp(alpha + k * sign(error), 0.05, 0.5) where k small. keep config in infra so we can tweak without deploy.
Priya: agree. config knobs: forecast_alpha, burst_pct, lease_ttl_s, fallback_cooldown_s. keep defaults but allow tenant override.
Mina: I'll draft a minimal RFC that outlines the intent schema, operator API, and metrics. will include a short rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> all).
Sam: action items: Mina RFC, Taylor add dashboards, Diego stub operator accept API, Priya wire up intent emitter in forecast service. I'll own the rollout checklist.
Priya: ping @orch-bot when the canary is ready so we can validate traces.
orch-bot: noted. will post canary trace links when canary telemetry shows >100 intents.
Taylor: linking the dashboard PR once up.
Mina: RFC draft in a bit, will tag reviewers (Sam, Diego, Priya). :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks all. short follow-up in ~24h after Taylor and Diego's changes land.
Sam: thanks — will keep an eye on the canary.
orch-bot: deploy-bot: forecast-service v2.3.1 promoted to canary cluster (p-dedicated-canary-7).
